objective: Enumerate each balanced round-bracket string once in lexicographic order with output-sensitive work.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Output size is a necessary part of enumeration cost.

defects: The input bound and fresh result ownership were unstated.
Time proportional to answers omitted the cost of constructing every output character.
Reference prefix strings and senior queued strings did not support a clear linear extra-space claim.
The11-pair case checked only length and endpoints, not every middle result.
rationale: Define integer pairs0..11, fresh mutable output and n/C_n input/output sizes. Author O(n * C_n) construction time and O(n) extra storage excluding output. Replace reference prefix strings and senior queued-prefix strings with one mutable buffer and O(n) call/explicit frames; retain the already-correct junior buffer board. Update skeleton/approach. Add three hidden assertions: independent exhaustive binary-string oracle for0..6 (5461 candidates), validity/strict order/completeness count of all58786 strings for11, and repeated-call array independence including mutation/zero pairs. A remaining-count backtracker passes; a shared cached output passed the old checks but now fails. Conservative recursive complexity remains unknown/unpenalized while the authored target is displayed.
